question: Assume today is 2026-09-11. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total number of passengers who used public transport in Spain in August 2026 (urban, interurban and special/discretionary transport combined), as it will be first reported in the provisional data of the National Statistics Institute's (INE) Passenger Transport Statistics (Estadística de Transporte de Personas).

target.what: Total number of passengers carried by public transport in Spain (urban, interurban and special/discretionary transport combined) during August 2026, as first reported in INE's Estadística de Transporte de Personas (ETP) provisional data
target.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE), Estadística de Transporte de Personas (ETP)
target.cadence: Monthly, provisional data released roughly two months after the reference month (August data typically published in October)
target.caveats: Target period is completed relative to cutoff (2026-09-11) but the August 2026 ETP release has not yet occurred, so no own-history for August 2026 exists. Working interpretation: total passengers (viajeros) across all public transport modes covered by ETP — urban (metro, bus), interurban (bus, rail,

candidates.hypothesis: August 2026 total ≈ August 2025 total × (1 + recent YoY growth rate). ETP monthly totals show strong August peaks; the most recent published months (June/July 2026) give the current YoY growth trend to extrapolate one month forward.
candidates.data_to_find: INE ETP monthly total passengers (all modes combined) for August 2024, August 2025, and the latest published months before cutoff (e.g., May–July 2026), plus YoY growth rates. Minimum: August 2025 total and the most recent 3 months' YoY growth.
search_hints: Estadística de Transporte de Personas INE viajeros agosto 2025
INE transporte de personas serie mensual viajeros total

candidates.hypothesis: Total = sum of urban (metro + bus), interurban (bus + rail + air + sea), and special/discretionary passengers. Each mode has its own August seasonal factor and growth trend; summing mode-level August 2026 estimates constrains the total and reveals which component drives uncertainty.
candidates.data_to_find: ETP mode-level monthly passenger series (metro, urban bus, interurban bus, rail/RENFE, air, sea, special/discretionary) for August 2025 and recent 2026 months, with YoY growth per mode.

candidates.hypothesis: Air passengers (Aena) and rail passengers (RENFE/AVE) dominate interurban totals; August 2026 air traffic can be estimated from Aena monthly statistics or flight schedules × load factor, then bridged to ETP air passenger count.
candidates.data_to_find: Aena August 2026 passenger statistics (or July 2026 as proxy), average load factors, and the ratio of ETP-reported air passengers to Aena total passengers.

candidates.hypothesis: August is the peak month; the August/July and August/annual ratios are stable year to year. Applying historical August seasonal factors to a 2026 annual or July 2026 base yields an August 2026 estimate.

With a level plus the 2.6% August 2025 growth and the recent monthly trend, a yoy_scaling route becomes executable and would dominate the current growth-only extrapolation.

kept.name: August 2026 vs August 2025 growth factor for total public transport passengers
kept.rationale: Anchored on the April 2026 INE total growth of +6.1% (p43) and the August 2025 total growth of +2.6% (p1). kept.applies_when: The 2026 monthly growth trend observed in April persists through August with normal August seasonality.
kept.falsified_by: A published June/July 2026 ETP total showing growth well below 2% or above 8%, or a major transport disruption in August 2026.

kept.name: August 2026 vs August 2025 growth factor for urban transport passengers
kept.rationale: Urban transport grew 8.4% in April 2026 (p44) and 4.0% in August 2025 (p2); August urban growth is typically lower than spring, so the factor is set between them, closer to the August 2025 rate.
kept.applies_when: Urban metro/bus demand growth in August 2026 is between the August 2025 and April 2026 rates.
kept.falsified_by: Operator data (Madrid/Barcelona metro, EMT) showing urban ridership flat or falling in August 2026.

kept.name: August 2026 vs August 2025 growth factor for interurban transport passengers
kept.rationale: Interurban grew only 1.2% in April 2026 (p45) and fell 1.4% in August 2025 (p38); rail liberalisation and tourism support modest growth, so the factor is set slightly above 1.
kept.applies_when: Interurban demand grows modestly in August 2026, consistent with the April 2026 trend.
kept.falsified_by: Aena/RENFE August 2026 data showing interurban passenger declines.

kept.name: August 2026 vs August 2025 growth factor for special and discretionary transport passengers
kept.rationale: Special/discretionary grew 6.1% in April 2026 (p46) and 11.7% in August 2025 (p3); August is the peak discretionary month, so the factor is set between the two rates.
kept.applies_when: Discretionary/tourism-linked transport continues to grow in August 2026 at a rate between the April 2026 and August 2025 rates.
kept.falsified_by: Tourism arrival data (Frontur) showing a summer 2026 decline, or operator reports of weaker coach/charter demand.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
